object_description: deep monolithic comb building with an entrance pavilion
design_condition: The building is placed parallel to the Allée des Marais with western access through the perimeter wall, while compact logistical circulation frees space for walks and sports fields.

positive.statement: The generous circulation areas, including expanded division corridors, provide overhead natural light.
The surrounding wall is carefully treated to reduce its impact on the landscape and life within the establishment.
Differentiated walking courses support resocialization and contribute to the quality of integration in the environment.
The comb organization offers a good response to users and is intelligently developed with interesting elements.
Logistical circulation is resolved compactly, freeing maximum space for walks and sports fields.
The phasing is well thought out, with consistent traffic flows from the first phase and limited contact surfaces between phases.

negative.statement: The juxtaposition of parallel circulations makes the central body too deep and harms the clarity of the project.
The result is a monolithic complex whose form is poorly defined and whose scale is not fully consistent with the penitentiary centre.
The cells face one another and do not provide truly clear views of the landscape.
The angled vertical sunshades strongly limit natural light entering the cells.
The proposed landscaping outside the walls does not really contribute to the quality of life of the establishment.
The total surface area is much greater than the target, raising questions about the general economics of the project.
Internal circulation weighs on the economy and flexibility of the project.
The relevance of the flood treatment and the safety of hollow elements still require confirmation.
